metadata.title: Pharaoh Brown - Signed to 53-man roster Tuesday
metadata.description: Brown was signed to the 53-man roster Tuesday.
metadata.analysis: Brown is currently listed on the depth chart behind Tyler Warren, Mo Alie-Cox and Drew Ogletree, so it doesn't appear he will have a prominent role anytime soon. The 32-year-old has played for the Browns, Texans, Patriots, Seahawks and Cardinals since entering the NFL in 2017, totaling 74 catches (102 targets) for 752 yards and three touchdowns in 92 regular-season appearances.

metadata.title: Pharaoh Brown signs with Colts 53-man roster
metadata.description: The Colts signed TE Pharaoh Brown to the 53-man roster from the practice squad.
metadata.analysis: Brown will add depth in the Colts tight end room.

metadata.title: Pharaoh Brown - Joins Colts' practice squad
metadata.description: Brown was signed to the Colts practice squad Monday.
metadata.analysis: Brown didn't make the Colts' 53-man roster but will at least remain with the team as a member of the practice squad. The 32-year-old has an extensive NFL resume, suiting up for the Browns, Texans, Patriots, Seahawks and Cardinals throughout his career and catching 74 passes for 752 yards and three touchdowns across 92 regular-season games.

metadata.title: Pharaoh Brown - Cut by Colts
metadata.description: Brown was released by the Colts on Sunday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
metadata.analysis: Brown was facing an uphill battle to make the roster as he had just signed with the team earlier this month. The 32-year-old spent last season with the Cardinals, catching both of his targets for one yard across seven games. Brown will now look to catch on with another team.

metadata.title: Pharaoh Brown released by Colts
metadata.description: The Colts released TE Pharaoh Brown.
metadata.analysis: Brown could land back on the practice squad of Indianapolis.

metadata.title: Pharaoh Brown signs with Colts
metadata.description: The Colts signed TE Pharaoh Brown.
metadata.analysis: Brown appeared in seven games with the Cardinals last season. He'll complete for a depth role in the Colts tight end room.

metadata.title: Pharaoh Brown - Signs with Indianapolis
metadata.description: The Colts signed Brown to a contract Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Brown played in seven games for the Cardinals last season, accumulating two receptions on two targets for one yard over 59 offensive snaps. The tight end also made special teams contributions over the seven-game span, participating in 77 snaps for the unit. The Colts placed fellow tight end Sean McKeon (undisclosed) on IR in a corresponding move.

metadata.title: Pharaoh Brown - Logs seven appearances in 2025
metadata.description: Brown reeled in both of his targets for one yard in seven regular-season appearances in 2025.
metadata.analysis: Brown spent the offseason and preseason with the Dolphins before getting released during roster cut downs in late August. He then joined the Cardinals in mid-October after TEs Tip Reiman (ankle) and Travis Vokolek (neck) landed on injured reserve. Arizona used its three elevations on him before he was signed to the active roster for good in early December, but he remained well behind Trey McBride, Elijah Higgins and Josiah Deguara in the pecking order for offensive snaps. Brown is an unrestricted free agent this offseason, so it remains to be seen where he'll be plying his wares in 2026.

metadata.title: Pharaoh Brown - Healthy scratch Week 17
metadata.description: Brown (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bengals, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Brown hasn't been used heavily in the offense this season, and he will observe Sunday's game from the sidelines while the Cardinals go with three active tight ends in Trey McBride, Elijah Higgins and Josiah Deguara. Brown's last opportunity to play this season is Week 18 against the Rams.

metadata.title: Pharaoh Brown - No targets in Week 16
metadata.description: Brown went without a target while playing seven of the Cardinals' 57 snaps on offense in Sunday's 26-19 loss to the Falcons.
metadata.analysis: Quarterback Jacoby Brissett targeted tight ends on 17 of his 31 pass attempts Sunday, but the bulk of those looks went to Trey McBride (4-27-0 receiving line on eight targets) and Elijah Higgins (7-91-0 on eight targets). Brown and Josiah Deguara (no catches on one target), meanwhile, remained afterthoughts on offense, which is expected to remain par for the course over the final two games of the season, barring an injury to either McBride or Higgins.
